transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (Pioneer Analytics - Head of ML), Mei Chen (Infra Lead), Rohan Desai (CTO, joined late)
Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/optimize-quant-profiles.pdf
Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/quant-profiles-playbook.xlsx

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on INT8 vs FP8 quantization profiles, quality vs latency tradeoffs, and pilot next steps. Customer cares about 95th p99 latency targets for chat use case, token-level cost savings, and traceability for audits.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll run through the quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize, show quality vs latency graphs, then talk pilot details.
[00:18] Carlos: Great, yeah we're really focused on bringing down inference cost without breaking the user experience. Our chat product needs p95 < 300ms for typical 512-token context and p99 ideally < 600ms.
[00:35] Maya: Awesome, that aligns with what we've seen with other customers. we'll show INT8 and FP8 profiles, typical quality deltas at sample prompts, and how caching + batching interacts.
[01:05] Mei: Quick infra note — we run on a mix of on-prem A100s and GCP T4s for burst. we care about deterministic behavior and audit logs.
[01:20] Jordan: Perfect — security and auditability are supported in our Private deployment; we have KMS integrations and detailed audit logs. we'll attach SOC2 docs after.
[02:02] Maya: Jumping into the console — (brief screen noise) — so here's the Optimize tab, quant profiles for model variants. For FP16 baseline, then FP8 fast profile, and INT8 aggressive. FP8 tends to give the best latency/quality sweet spot on recent transformer variants.
[03:00] Carlos: When you say FP8, do you mean block FP8 or per-channel? we had issues with some quant libs before.
[03:18] Maya: Good q — Redwood uses per-tensor calibration with per-layer fallback; the Optimize playbook includes calibration scripts. there are edge cases where we fall back to FP16 on attention layers.
[04:00] Mei: Can you share typical numbers? like latency improvements and quality loss as measured by our evals?
[04:18] Maya: Sure — on a 512-context, FP8 profile shaved about 28-35% off latency vs FP16 on A100s in our lab runs, INT8 got up to 50% CPU/GPU throughput improvement but with a noticeable quality delta on longer open-ended prompts. p99s improved but variance increased for INT8.
[05:10] Jordan: Example numbers we showed in the deck: FP16 baseline p95 = 270ms, FP8 p95 = 200ms, INT8 p95 = 150ms. p99s were 520/370/320 respectively in one sample. quality drop (measured by our eval BLEU/ROUGE style proxy + human spot checks) was ~1-2% for FP8 and ~4-7% for INT8 on creative prompts.
[06:05] Carlos: That 4-7% on creative stuff is our worry. our QA measures show user-visible hallucinations at that range.
[06:22] Maya: Absolutely — that's why we recommend a tiered routing policy: host FP8 for most traffic, INT8 for low-cost batch jobs or less safety-critical paths, and FP16 for canary or high-accuracy flows.
[07:10] Mei: how about rollout and canaries? we need to be able to rollback fast if quality regresses.
[07:28] Jordan: Console supports canary rollouts per route and automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity variant if latencies or quality metrics degrade past thresholds. we also log token-level diffs and evaluation markers.
[08:05] Rohan (joined): Sorry I'm late — quick context, cost is important but uptime and predictability even more. what's the SLA on these dedicated profiles?
[08:20] Maya: For Dedicated we offer reserved capacity and SLA-backed latency windows; for private deployments we partner on operational SLOs. tuning quantization doesn't change the SLA commitment — it's a model runtime config.
[09:00] Carlos: On the dataset side — we'll share our 2000 prompt eval set. you'll run Optimize profiles against it?
[09:12] Maya: Yes, we'll run the full battery: quality metrics, latency distributions, token-cost delta, and we can produce a per-prompt heatmap showing where INT8 diverges.
[10:00] Jordan: Also want to flag caching — prefix/KV cache can dramatically reduce tokens for multi-turn chat. if you leverage prefix cache + FP8 you might hit cost targets without needing INT8.
[10:30] Mei: We saw caching help a lot on standard sessions, but our support for long-form summaries means some sessions still hit long contexts.
[11:05] Maya: For long contexts, INT8 sometimes amplifies generation artifacts; we usually prefer FP8 with selective INT8 on MLP layers only — it's a hybrid profile.
[12:00] Carlos: Are these hybrid profiles easy to manage from API? we don't want dozens of variants.
[12:18] Maya: You can define a profile and expose it as a model variant in the model catalog; routing policies can map routes to variants. so it's manageable.
[13:00] Jordan: Pricing note — token-level unit costs drop with quantization because of higher throughput; we'll share a modeled projection in the benchmark spreadsheet for your expected qps.
[14:00] Carlos: For the pilot, we want to validate p95/p99 on our infra. can Redwood run perf tests on our on-prem A100s?
[14:18] Maya: Yes — we can run a pilot perf run. we'll need ssh access or a small agent and a stable test harness. planning note: schedule a 2-hour window during low production.
[15:00] Mei: Security — you said SOC2, KMS. Do you also provide VPC peering for private control plane?
[15:18] Jordan: For Private deployments we support VPC peering, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and audit logs retained per your retention policy. we'll attach details.
[16:00] Carlos: Competitors question — we've talked to X and Y; how do you compare to the big cloud vendors on quant support?
[16:12] Maya: We focus on production-first tooling and operational controls: the difference is the Optimize playbook + routing + canary controls and built-in evals tied to rollouts. some vendors give kernels but not the ops layer.
[17:00] Rohan: Any gotchas with batching? our request patterns are spiky.
[17:20] Maya: Redwood's continuous batching helps smooth spiky traffic; there are latency tradeoffs. with spiky traffic we suggest smaller max-batch sizes and lower batching windows to hit p95 targets.
[18:00] Carlos: Could you show a quality vs latency chart quick?
[18:12] Maya: (screen noise) here's a chart from the deck — x-axis latency, y-axis quality score. you can see FP8 sits near the knee — moderate latency drop with minimal quality regression. INT8 pushes left further but with larger quality loss on open prompts.
[20:00] Carlos: That matches what we feared. For chat-sessions we'd probably prefer FP8 + caching. For background summarization jobs maybe INT8.
[20:20] Maya: Exactly — that's the common pattern. we also recommend automated regression alerts tied to your eval rubric so you catch issues immediately.
[22:00] Jordan: Next steps recap: I'll send the spreadsheet and SOC2/security pack. Maya will book the pilot perf run and run the initial quant evaluations against your sample prompts.
[22:30] Mei: we'll confirm the dataset and preferred pilot window by Friday.
[23:00] Carlos: One more question — saving quantization profiles for audits, do you store calibration snapshots?
[23:15] Maya: Yes, Optimize stores calibration artifacts and provenance metadata so you can audit which calibration and hyperparams were used for a given model variant.
[25:00] Rohan: on the ROI side, what kind of payback have other customers seen?
[25:18] Jordan: Typical unit-cost reduction of 20-40% with FP8 and up to 60% in INT8-heavy setups, depending on throughput and caching. customers often recover quant-tuning effort in 6-10 weeks for high-volume apps.
[28:00] Carlos: If we do the pilot and it's promising, timeline to get Dedicated reserved capacity?
[28:12] Jordan: For Dedicated, we have a procurement flow — once pilot confirms throughput and SLOs, draft an SOW and committed capacity can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks depending on region.
[30:00] Maya: (demo continues showing console steps) — how to create a quant profile, toggle layer-level fallbacks, run a batch eval, export results.
[35:00] Carlos: minor nit — some of our prompts have vendor-specific tokens, will that affect calibration?
[35:12] Maya: Calibration uses a representative corpus; include those tokens and we'll surface layer contributions so you can inspect divergence.
[38:00] Mei: do you support automatic rollback if quality drops post-rollout? can that be automated?
[38:12] Jordan: Yes — we can set policy to automatically re-route traffic to the previous variant or to a flagship FP16 variant if eval metrics cross thresholds.
[42:00] Carlos: sounds good. any documentation on the per-model quant callbacks?
[42:12] Maya: We'll share the Optimize playbook and the calibration scripts repo link in the follow-up.
[45:00] Jordan: ok wrapping up. quick recap of action items and owners.
[45:20] Carlos: thanks, this was useful.
[46:00] Rohan: Appreciate it. we'll aim to confirm dataset and window by Friday.
[46:30] Jordan: Perfect, we'll follow up with the links and schedule. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
